findings.evidence: The proof at :504-505 is `rw [coe_peterWeylBasis, peterWeylFamily_apply, ContRepresentation.matrixCoeffLp_def, map_smul]`; `matrixCoeffLp_def` (Compact/MatrixCoefficient.lean:79, `:= (rfl)`) and `peterWeylFamily_apply` (:381) carry no `IsAlgClosed`/skeleton hypothesis. `stdPeterWeylBasis_apply` (:717-718) is `simpa only [stdPeterWeylBasis]` over the same lemma. findings.issue: `peterWeylBasis_apply` (:496) and `stdPeterWeylBasis_apply` (:708) duplicate content already available from `coe_peterWeylBasis`/`coe_stdPeterWeylBasis` plus `peterWeylFamily_apply` and `ContRepresentation.matrixCoeffLp_def`, and gate it behind `[IsAlgClosed 𝕜]` and `IsIrrepSkeleton models`, which the identity does not use. Their LHS is also not simp-normal: `@[simp] coe_peterWeylBasis` (:489) and `@[simp] coe_stdPeterWeylBasis` (:701) rewrite `peterWeylBasis h x` / `stdPeterWeylBasis 𝕜 G x` away, so neither lemma fires on a simp-normalized goal.

summary: The coefficient layer is now correct: `peterWeylCoeff_def` restores access to the unexposed body and `peterWeylCoeff_eq_inner` characterizes it with no skeleton or algebraic-closedness hypothesis, and the standard layer no longer duplicates the general lemmas. What remains is the pair of `_apply` bridges, which restate existing unconditional content behind `[IsAlgClosed 𝕜]` plus a skeleton.
